critical.finding: The key risk and the bear story are not in the numbers: in all three scenarios the engine's FY2027 capex (maintenance + growth capex) drops to about 84B (bear 26.8+57.1), 97.5B (base 28.5+69.0) and 104B (bull 29.9+74.3), a 25-40% cut from the guided 135-145B of 2026 (9M 2026 purchases of property and equipment 83.06B, 10-Q 2026-10-22). Nothing in the evidence supports a cut: the 2027 capex outlook comes only at the Q4 call, non-cancelable commitments due 2027 are 121.41B and 355.73B of leases not yet commenced start through 2036. The bear event explicitly says capex keeps rising in 2027 while the bear drivers cut it the most (sales_to_capital 0.55 on smaller revenue growth). The model's what_must_be_true confirms the blind spot: the capital_efficiency lever is not_reachable (value stays 861-1,063 across 0-6x growth investment), so the decisive risk the table names cannot move the fair value of 875.
